notes: Vals AI boards for Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, board metadata updated 2026-10-12, read 2026-10-13. Vals added both models on 2026-10-12 (it calls them 'Wonder' and 'Wonder Full') and ran both at reasoning effort max. Rows are the 'overall' task of 18 benchmark views (Vals Index, Finance Agent v2, Terminal-Bench 4.0, Terminal-Bench Science, Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, ProgramBench, SWE-bench Multimodal, BioMysteryBench, CyberBench v1.1, EMB, Code Migration, Legal Research Bench, MysteryMechanism, ProofBench v1.1, Public Benefits Bench v1.1, Tax Agent Bench, Vibe Code Bench v1.1, IOI) read from each page's board view JSON; same-snapshot rows for Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh and max) are stored for every benchmark where they have a row. Accuracy is converted from percent to a 0-1 fraction; stderr and cost per test are as published; cost per test is USD per test. Effort is the board payload's reasoning_effort (non-Anthropic) or compute_effort (Anthropic) field; every stored row states one. Every stored accuracy and stderr was cross-checked against the rendered Vals model-page tables (no differences). Vals' displayed ranks differ from ordering the board JSON by accuracy for some rows (ties, hidden models), so ranks are not stored except where quoted from Vals' own text in claims. The Terminal-Bench views state the Mini-SWE-agent harness; the other views state none. Rows are comparable:false and each board has its own comparability group. Peer values for the Vals Index, Finance Agent v2 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 equal the 2026-10-06 Vals snapshot values already in the pack (Vals did not re-score them); Claude Haiku 5.5 rows are new on Vals since the 2026-10-07 coverage file recorded it absent on the Vals Index and Terminal-Bench 4.0 boards. Recheck on or after 2026-10-20.

claims.statement: Vals AI update note on both model pages, verbatim: 'Wonder Full places #5 of 47 on the Vals Index (64.57%) at $8.56 per test. Wonder places #10 (61.06%). Wonder is #1 of 47 on CyberBench (80.36%). Wonder Full is #3 on Public Benefits Bench (73.75%) and #4 on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark (21.67%). Both models are priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, and were run with reasoning effort set to "max".' Vals hyperparameters on the pages: temperature 1, top-p and top-k default, max output tokens 131,072, reasoning effort max, default provider Meta; fallback rate 0.00% for both; refusal rate 0.22% (Wonder) and 0.04% (Wonder Full).
claims.implication: Both models were run at max on Vals. Vals published no lower-effort run, so there is no Vals evidence below max.

claims.statement: Vals Index (board updated 2026-10-12, 47 models), all at max unless noted: Sonnet 5.5 67.04% ($21.34/test), Opus 5.5 66.97% ($32.14), Fable 5.1 65.83% ($28.71), Muse Wonder Full 64.57% ($8.56), GPT-6 Astra 63.12% ($18.46), GPT-6.1 Sol 61.15% ($3.24), Muse Wonder 61.06% ($11.43), Muse Spark 1.3 max 58.16% ($3.79; xhigh 53.20%), Haiku 5.5 54.31% ($2.99). Cost per test is Vals' figure; Opus 5.5 costs about 3.8x Muse Wonder Full per test for 2.4 index points more.
claims.implication: Muse Wonder Full is 5th on Vals, behind Gemini 4 Argon (68.90%, not a catalog model), Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1; Muse Wonder is 10th and level with GPT-6.1 Sol within the 1.0 pp standard error. Vals Index is a mixed composite; do not treat it as a coding score.

claims.statement: Where the Muse models lead or trail on Vals (accuracy %, max effort): CyberBench v1.1 Muse Wonder 80.4, Haiku 5.5 75.5, Muse Wonder Full 73.6, Opus 5.5 55.4, Astra 41.1; Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark Muse Wonder Full 21.7, Wonder 17.1, Muse Spark 1.3 max 23.8, Opus 5.5 3.8; Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Mini-SWE-agent) Opus 5.5 65.2, Sonnet 5.5 64.1, Astra 59.6, Muse Wonder Full 58.1, GPT-6.1 Sol 55.1, Muse Wonder 49.5; IOI Astra 100.0, Sol 96.9, Opus 5.5 95.1, Muse Wonder Full 79.8, Wonder 66.9; ProofBench Opus 5.5 100.0, Muse Wonder Full 94.0, Wonder 84.0; SWE-bench Multimodal Opus 5.5 70.2, Muse Wonder Full 47.3; ProgramBench Opus 5.5 18.5, Muse Wonder Full 0.5; Terminal-Bench Science Astra 62.9, Sol 52.9, Opus 5.5 47.1, Muse Wonder 22.9 (no Muse Wonder Full row).
claims.implication: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full are ahead of Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol on Vals Harvey (Muse Spark 1.3 max, 23.75, is higher still) and Muse Wonder is first on CyberBench; both trail Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on Terminal-Bench 4.0, IOI, ProofBench, SWE-bench Multimodal, ProgramBench and Terminal-Bench Science. Per-benchmark rows are in the score list.

claims.statement: CONFLICTS between Vals, Artificial Analysis and Meta for the same benchmark name, stored side by side and not reconciled: Terminal-Bench 4.0: Vals (Mini-SWE-agent harness) Muse Wonder Full 58.1%, Wonder 49.5%, Opus 5.5 65.2%; AA Intelligence Index Terminal-Bench 4.0 gives Muse Wonder Full 57.1%, Wonder 52.0%, Opus 5.5 59.6% (and Meta's table 'Terminal-Bench 4.0-AA' repeats 57.1 and 52.0); the AA Coding Agents run gives 59.1%, 47.5%, 63.1%. Harvey: Vals HLAB Muse Wonder Full 21.67% and Opus 5.5 3.75% against AA's Harvey LAB-AA 13.06% and 4.17% (Meta's table: 13.1 and 4.2). Finance Agent v2: Vals Muse Wonder Full 59.06%, Wonder 56.64%, Fable 5.1 58.88%, Opus 5.5 58.59%, Astra 53.54% against Meta's table 59.1, 56.6, 58.9, 58.6, 53.5 (agree to one decimal).
claims.implication: Do not average across boards. The Vals and AA harnesses differ (Mini-SWE-agent vs AA-run agents), which moves Opus 5.5 by 5.6 points and Muse Wonder Full by 1.0 on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

claims.statement: Vals prices both Muse Wonder models at $4/$20 per M tokens on its model pages, including Muse Wonder Full, which Meta sells only through the Muse Code subscription and for which AA states 'Muse Wonder Full is not priced per token'. Vals' cost per test for Muse Wonder Full ($8.56 on the Vals Index, $10.53 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, $2.39 on Finance Agent v2) is therefore a computed figure at Muse Wonder's list price, not a billed price. Modality difference: Vals lists video input as not supported for Muse Wonder (supported for Muse Wonder Full) and file input as supported for both; AA and OpenRouter list video input for Muse Wonder.
claims.implication: Treat Vals cost for Muse Wonder Full as illustrative. Not reconciled with the Meta lane facts.
